title: vetted.json: one vetting decision per candidate
description: Written by the vetting step into the hunt dir. scripts/verdict.py admissibility() decides what reaches the author; the model's decision can downgrade a row but never upgrade it. Enum values are the tokens in scripts/verdicts.py.

id.description: Test id (path::TestName) for A/B/D/old rows, or the CodeRabbit claim id (CR1..) for R rows. Looked up in base_<tag>.json, review_verdicts.json, diff_D.json or old_tests.json.

source.description: Mode that produced the candidate. old = existing test on new code. verify = /verify UI or API compare. V and verify are both accepted; neither has a mechanical verdict yet, so such rows are always held.

decision.description: Model decision. KEEP is necessary but not sufficient for the author.

reason.description: One or two sentences: why the decision was made.

caller.description: The real caller (HTTP route, websocket handler, plugin API, UI) that reaches the input, or a note that none does.

entry_point.description: Real entry point the reproduction goes through, e.g. "api4 DELETE /api/v4/x" or "verify plan path". Null when the finding is not reproduced through an entry point; such a row is always held.

repro_cmd.description: One shell command that reproduces the failure. Empty means held.

evidence_path.description: Path to the artifact that backs the decision (run log, base_<tag>.json, diff_D.examples.json, ...).

fix_check.description: Result of the fix-commit check, or null when no fix exists. STRICTLY_WEAK means the test fails on the fix too, so the row is held.

reason_code.description: Kind of evidence behind the decision. KEEP: BUG. DROP: INTENDED, UNREACHABLE or WRONG_ASSERTION, checked by verdict.check_drop. HELD: NEEDS_INPUT. A DROP without a checkable code is held.

evidence_quote.description: Verbatim text backing the decision: from the PR description, diff or pr_tests_diff (INTENDED), the diff or a caller (UNREACHABLE), or the candidate's test source (WRONG_ASSERTION).
